text:
nadia: Heads-up - after flipping the new kernel-selector heuristic to canary were seeing host CPU tail climb. Looks like parsing + many small writes are the offender, not decode.

sam: can you share the quick profile?

oliver: snip from a 30s perf sample on the canary box:
```
# perf top -p <pid>
 25.7% tokenize::parse_tokens
 18.4% http2::hpack_encode
 12.9% streamer::emit_small_frame
 10.2% kv::move_shard
 5.8% grpc::writev
```

rita: kv::move_shard is the red flag - the kernel placement is causing requests to hit different KV shard owners and were seeing increased evicts and remaps during warmup.

nadia: Repro locally with a short-seq workload (1.5k rps): when selector prefers "ultra-fast" kernels the average # of write syscalls per request goes from ~1.1 -> ~3.7 and kv-hit drops ~9% for the first 60s.

sam: hypothesis: selector is optimizing for per-request latency but ignoring KV locality/warmth. The cheaper kernel may live on a worker without the shard resident, leading to more cache churn and extra proto unmarshalling.

oliver: two low-risk mitigations to test quickly: 1) affinity-lock: during session warmup prefer kernels that already have the request's KV shard pinned for N requests; 2) ingress frame coalescer: coalesce up to M tiny token frames into a single write within T ms.

rita: agree. also consider batching watermark tweak for short sequences (raise threshold so we collect slightly larger mini-batches before kernel assignment).

nadia: plan of attack: rollback the rollout on canary for 30m while we iterate. Then run an A/B: group A = v2 as-is, group B = v2 + affinity-lock + ingress-coalesce flag. We'll monitor host CPU, writev syscalls/sec, kv-evict-rate, and p50/p95 latency.

sam: I'll roll rollback now and keep the canary stable.

perf-bot: [alert] Kernel-selector v2 canary -> host CPU p99 +10%, kv-evict-rate +7%, writev syscall rate +180%. Trace: 3123459999. Suggested test points: affinity, coalesce, batch watermark.

oliver: prototyping affinity-lock: keep a soft pin for the first 16 requests of a flow. Configurable and disabled by default. Also adding metrics: kernel->kv_shard hit ratio and shard residency count per kernel.

rita: ingress coalescer config I'll try: max_frames=5, max_delay_ms=2, max_merged_bytes=4096. Should reduce syscall rate a lot; need to check single-request p50 overhead. We'll gate by p95 not regressing by >5%.

nadia: important: add a rollout-time alert if kv-evict-rate increases >5% and another if writev/sec increases >100% vs baseline. Also surface hpck encode ops in the per-canary flame dashboard.

sam: rollback done. early metrics: host p95 back to baseline within 7m. Holding canary for 20m then starting A/B.

oliver: load tests ready. Ill run a 10min experiment with 2k short requests/s and capture flamegraphs, syscall traces, and tcpdump to confirm HPACK reductions.

rita: note — coalescing will slightly increase p50 for single-request flows (we buffer up to 2ms). But if it cuts p95/p99 host CPU and reduces kv-evicts, overall user-visible tail should improve. We'll only enable it if p95 remains within the allowed window.

perf-bot: [note] Created ticket PERF-1420 "kernel-selector: warmup affinity + ingress coalescer" and attached initial perf snapshot.

nadia: thanks team. Postmortem/sync tomorrow 2026-03-24 16:00 UTC. Bring runtime owners, ingress, and perf. Keep updates in-thread. :thumbsup:
